title: Silicon Valley leaders call for reinstatement of Nvidia CEO with 'Stand With Jensen' petition
summary: A petition calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is drawing support from prominent Silicon Valley personalities, four days after his resignation stemming from revelations of multiple…

image.caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks after attending the AI Ecosystem Reception in Tokyo, on July 16. (Manami Yamada/Reuters)

blocks.text: Business·New

A petition calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is drawing support from prominent Silicon Valley personalities, four days after his resignation stemming from revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy.
Signatories include Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney

More than 179,000 people had signed the petition, according to the website hosting it. Those listed as signatories included Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, Replit CEO Amjad Masad and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.
Nvidia shares suffered early losses, but remained more than one per cent lower after U.S. President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang return as CEO.
"I think he learned a big lesson," Trump said.

The Stand With Jensen website coincided with an open letter from two prominent investors, Atreides Management's Gavin Baker and Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, who urged Nvidia's board to avoid rushing to replace Huang before all the facts were known.

"We are current and former NVIDIA employees, partners, shareholders, and supporters. We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the Board: bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA's best interests," according to an open letter published on the website.

The website showed that more than 8,400 signatories identified themselves as current Nvidia employees, claiming this represents approximately 21 per cent of all Nvidia employees. A further 94,000 signatories identified themselves as shareholders, although the website cautioned that professional affiliations were self-reported and had not been independently verified.
Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO

The campaign comes as some prominent investors also urge Nvidia's board not to rush to replace Huang. Atreides Management's Gavin Baker and Altimeter Capital Management CEO Brad Gerstner said in an open letter that the board should wait until all the facts were known.
Shockwaves through industry

Huang stepped down on Thursday after reports of alleged affairs with employees, including one who reported directly to him, plunging the AI chip heavyweight into crisis and sending shockwaves through an industry he helped bankroll.

Corporate boards have previously removed chief executives over relationships with employees. McDonald's fired Steve Easterbrook in 2019 over a consensual relationship with an employee that violated company policy, while Intel CEO Brian Krzanich resigned in 2018 after a similar policy breach.

Could Nvidia survive without its ultra-powerful CEO, Jensen Huang?

blocks.text: But the episode also highlights the challenges boards can face when ousting high-profile executives who retain strong employee and investor backing. OpenAI reinstated Sam Altman as CEO in November 2023, just days after his removal triggered an employee revolt and opposition from investors.
The turmoil at Nvidia comes as the company is taking on growing strategic importance in Washington.
Is the Nvidia scandal fracturing Trump's administration?

Trump's reported trades this year suggest he held between $13 million US and $62 million US in Nvidia stock as of the end of August, the Washington Post reported on Monday, citing a review of his financial disclosures.
The Trump administration also plans to designate Nvidia and more than two dozen other AI companies as "national champions," the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for Nvidia to appoint an outsider as its next CEO, saying the company needs a "dramatic shakeup" following Huang's departure.
Colette Kress was named interim CEO in the wake of Huang’s resignation. She previously served as executive vice-president and chief financial officer.
The website hosting the petition included a call to institutional investors to dial into an earnings call slated for Tuesday and raise the issue of Huang’s ousting.
